newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila overnight money steady in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: Manila overnight money steady in liquid market.

text.p: Manila overnight money was steady at an average of 10.5625 percent on Tuesday amid high liquidity in the market, traders said.
The Central Bank prevented rates from falling through its overnight borrowing rate of 10.5 percent.
Rates were locked in a tight band from 10.75 to 10.53125 percent, with 29 lenders and 24 borrowers.
Volume fell to 16.431 billion from 17.297 billion pesos.
"There is no driving force to have a spike in rates. We expect interest rates to be flat for a while," a trader said.
Traders said banks are expected to be more liquid after the Central Bank withdrew its four-day reverse repo instrument because its maturity would fall on a weekend.
They added, however, the Central Bank may offer it again soon. The Central Bank has been offering reverse repos of five days or less because these are not subject to the new 20 percent tax.
Meanwhile, banks, awash with liquidity, were buying short-term bills at the secondary market, traders said.
A Reuter poll of seven institutions showed bid rates of 10.60 to 10.725 for three-month bills; 11.00 to 11.15 for six months; and 11.50 to 11.60 for one year.
